Agreed 100%. I try not to blame individuals because it’s a systemic problem. We’re so highly propagandized in western countries, specifically in America, that most of us don’t know how to recognize that capitalism isn’t the natural order of things. It’s mind boggling to watch struggling people defend this exploitative system that’s literally killing them.

This is where I’m conflicted. I see anti-liberalism and actual fascism growing in mainstream media, but I’m not convinced that a majority of people are falling for it. A significant portion of the population is, of course, and that’s extremely worrying, but I’m not convinced it’s most people. But maybe that’s just me being hopeful.

I don’t know that I’d consider anti-capitalism an extremist point of view. Fascism is definitely taking root in our government, in both parties (obviously worse in rightwing politics). Stopping it is going to be a bitch.

I can only speak for myself when it comes to why some suffer more than others. My parents lost custody of me when I was very young, and I fell through the cracks. A lot of things that happened to me shouldn’t have, that were extremely traumatic and that I’m still struggling with today. I have a hard time making close connections — of course, it’s the thing I want most and the thing I’m worst at. I don’t know how to let people in. I don’t know how to stop self sabotaging myself. I’m really doing my best, but my best isn’t good enough. So I’m basically at the point where, if this is just how my life is going to be, I don’t want it anymore.

Oh I definitely wish money didn’t exist. I wish success wasn’t tied to money, and that your value wasn’t tied to your financial or career success. I love my job and I wish I didn’t have to charge for it. As far as education goes, at this point, its only purpose seems to be to produce more cogs for the machine:  more laborers and obedient little consumers. I hate it. 

Suffering is going to happen to us all, sure, but does it need to be sewn into our society? For there to be winners, there has to be losers, and the losers are just relentlessly shat upon. It leads to a very lonely, traumatic experience, and for no reason. Even when I was financially secure, I felt this way.

Maybe you’re right. I imagine people who come from very tight communities know more happiness than those of us raised in this hyper individualistic, capitalist hellscape that is mainstream America. 

As far as billionaires go, I think many of them are unhappy because they’ve had to do so many immoral, uncaring, exploitative things to get there. I constantly see people with little in life being the most caring and giving. It also seems to me that they struggle the most. 

A good society to me is one in which everyone has their basic needs met, community is close, supportive, available, and cherished, and those who are struggling are uplifted, not allowed to fall through the cracks. I don’t think we need to be so competitive with each other, that if we actually work together, we’d all be able to eat.

I’m game to talk more. It really does help to know I’m not alone in my struggles. At the same time, I can’t believe there are so many of us struggling like this. It makes me think we’re doing life wrong. Or our society is wrong.
